locator.text: Equation (A.34), p. 138, in the proof of Lemma A.6

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same formula, assembled from one theorem plus three definitions and the coefficient lemma rather than displayed as one identity. Rewriting: put a = 1 + h (the Lean hypothesis is 1 < a, i.e. h > 0, as in the paper). iteratedDerivWithin_profile gives H^{(m)}(Z) = profileJet (1+h) m Z; unfolding profileJet, moment and kernel gives (Γ(1+h))⁻¹ · derivativeCoeff (1+h) m · ∫_{v>0} e^{-v} v^{(1+h)+m-1} (1+Zv)^{1-(1+h)-m} dv, and (1+h)+m-1 = h+m, 1-(1+h)-m = -h-m, so both exponents agree with the paper term for term; derivativeCoeff_eq_rising turns the coefficient into (-1)^m ∏_{k<m}(h+k) = (-1)^m (h)_m with the paper's own convention (b)_m = b(b+1)⋯(b+m-1), (b)_0 = 1 (AppendixHeatResults.rising, rising_zero, rising_succ). The normalisation Γ(a) = Γ(1+h) matches, the domain of integration Ioi 0 matches ∫_0^∞, and the derivative is one-sided on Ici 0 for Z ≥ 0 (iteratedDerivWithin_profile) and two-sided for Z > 0 (iteratedDeriv_profile), matching the paper's half-line statement. Non-vacuous: integrability of the kernel is proved separately (kernel_integrable, RadialHeatProfile.lean:69), so `moment` is a genuine integral and not a junk value.
